item.title: ‘He knows the consequences’: Trump warns Xi over Taiwan; declines to say if US would defend
item.description: President Trump stated that Chinese President Xi Jinping understands the consequences if China attacks Taiwan. He indicated that Beijing knows the repercussions and has previously stated they would not act while Trump is president. Trump declined to reveal specific details of his discussions with Xi, emphasizing that the other side is aware of the potential outcomes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Criticize me all you want': Kash Patel shields girlfriend Alexis Wilkins from trolling, says she's a true patriot
item.description: "Let me be clear: we will not be distracted by baseless rumors or the noise from uninformed internet anarchists and the fake news. I’ve always said — criticize me all you want. But going after the people doing great work, my personal life, or those around me is a total disgrace," Kash Patel said sending a strong message to trolls.

item.title: Young men from Ukraine increasingly coming to Germany
item.description: Ukraine has eased border restrictions for men aged 18-22, leading to a surge in their arrival in Germany. These young men, often well-educated, seek temporary protection to pursue studies or apprenticeships. While some face criticism, they view this as a vital opportunity for their future, with many hoping to contribute to both Germany and Ukraine.

item.title: PM Carney cites ‘progress’ with India, Asia-Pacific; seeks to cut US dependence
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney highlighted progress in building Asia-Pacific partnerships, including with India, as a strategy to reduce reliance on the United States amid escalating tariff tensions. He apologized to President Trump for a provincial anti-tariff ad, emphasizing federal control over trade policy. Carney expressed optimism for future US trade talks once conditions stabilize.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: Sneako calls out Erika Kirk for her viral hug with JD Vance and her bold Charlie Kirk comparison
item.description: A viral video shows Erika Kirk, widow of Charlie Kirk, hugging Vice President JD Vance at a Turning Point USA event. Kirk's speech comparing Vance to her late husband sparked debate, with a subsequent hug drawing widespread online commentary. Streamer Sneako's mocking remarks added to the controversy, making the incident a major political talking point.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: SNL’s ‘Weekend Update’ gets dark as Colin Jost mocks Trump’s Halloween clip
item.description: Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update delivered a shockwave with Colin Jost's controversial Donald Trump Halloween joke, referencing Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' and child abuse allegations. The edgy commentary, met with mixed audience reactions, highlighted SNL's history of pushing political satire boundaries. The segment also featured Bowen Yang's comedic return as George Santos, adding levity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Cameras analyzing my every move but...' Erika Kirk speaks up amid row over viral hug with JD Vance
item.description: Erika Kirk received a huge backlash for what commentators said was a lack of mourning period for her husband, as she jumped straight into work as she took up the new role as the CEO of TPUSA. Her hug to JD Vance went viral and so did her words as she said there were similarities between Charlie and JD.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What US school kids are learning about climate
item.description: Educators like Jeff Grant are increasingly teaching climate change science to high schoolers, a move supported by public demand. However, curriculum decisions vary widely across US school districts, with some teachers lacking adequate training and facing misinformation campaigns from fossil fuel interests. Making climate change relatable is key, especially in states with strong ties to these industries.

item.title: 'Enraged' Kash Patel 'fires' official who supervised FBI's aviation units amid row over his visit to girlfriend
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel reportedly became enraged after a supervisor of the agency's aviation units, Steven Palmer, was allegedly told to resign due to controversy surrounding Patel's personal travel. The controversy stemmed from Patel's use of an agency jet to attend his girlfriend's performance, a trip questioned by a former FBI agent.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why the Republican party is red — even thought red usually means the Left
item.description: In the U.S., red has become the color of the Republican Party, a media convention born from television graphics during the 2000 presidential election. This accidental branding, where red was assigned to Republicans and blue to Democrats, has since become a cultural shorthand for the nation's deep political polarization, despite red's global association with the Left.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Accomplished daughter of immigrants': Ro Khanna supports Usha Vance amid Hindu row, Meghan McCain says she's iconic
item.description: Second Lady Usha Vance received unexpected support from Congressman Ro Khanna and MAGA activist Meghan McCain amidst a controversy over her faith. Khanna defended her as an accomplished immigrant's daughter, while McCain highlighted Usha Vance's broad appeal and positive impact. Usha Vance, who is raising her children as Christians, stated she has no intention of converting.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'My Hindu ancestors were oppressed': Indian-origin Christian MAGA activist 'caught lying' in support of JD Vance
item.description: A controversy erupted after JD Vance expressed hope his Hindu wife would convert to Christianity. MAGA commentator Dinesh D'Souza defended Vance, claiming his own low-caste Hindu ancestors in India converted as they were treated badly. However, D'Souza was accused of contradicting his own writings about his Brahmin ancestry, leading to further debate on religious conversion and caste.

item.title: ‘Hindus realising Christian nationalists are not friends’: Mehdi Hasan weighs in on JD Vance’s remarks about wife Usha's religion
item.description: Journalist Mehdi Hasan commented on JD Vance's remarks about his Hindu wife's faith, suggesting conservative Hindus and Jews aligning with the MAGA movement are discovering Christian nationalists aren't allies. Vance's hope for his wife's conversion drew criticism, with the Hindu American Foundation urging reciprocal engagement. Vance defended his comments, calling backlash 'disgusting'.

item.title: ‘People hid in toilets’: Passengers thought stabbing was Halloween prank; how attack unfolded on London-bound train
item.description: A terrifying knife attack on a Saturday evening train from Doncaster to London near Huntingdon left ten people injured, nine critically. The incident, declared a major incident, has prompted a counter-terror investigation. Passengers described scenes of panic as armed officers boarded the train, arresting two suspects. Authorities are working to establish the motive behind the horrific event.
